A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) the India-Eurasian collision was not a sudden event but a gradual process; (2) the foreland basinal evolution of the eastern Xinghai basin was controlled by the India-Eurasial collision; (3) the foreland basin was formed in response to the tibetan plateau growth.

the Cretaceous-Paleogene foreland basin in the eastern Xinning basin developed in the time span from ca. 74 to 23 Ma, with the sedimentary hiatus of ∼19 m.y. from ca. 70 to 49 Ma, and the sedimentation was mainly controlled by the India-Eurasian collision in southern Tibet, which resulted in the growth of the West Qinling and Laji Shan.

the Cretaceous-Paleogene unconformity in the Xining basin is a major stratigraphic marker for the foreland basing evolution in response to the tibetan plateau building.
